meta.description: GALP.LS analysis: Galp raised its 2026 EBITDA guide by ~50% to €4bn and pays 3.4%: but the Namibia catalyst is spent and the market sold the print. B+, a diversifier to buy at 19.45, not at the highs.
meta.ogDescription: Galp guides €4bn EBITDA and yields 3.4% at 5.3x EV/EBITDA. Why the trade is at 19.45, and what the July fade really said.

verdict.summary: Galp did something rare in July: it raised its full-year EBITDA guidance by roughly 50%, from above €2.6bn to around €4bn, lifted operating cash flow guidance to ~€3bn and bumped the dividend 10% to €0.70. The market's answer was to sell the stock from 20.96 to 19.38 in two sessions. Both reactions make sense. The raise is real but macro-made; refining margins and price marks did most of it, and it landed next to a revenue miss and a slight EBITDA shortfall in the quarter itself. Meanwhile the Namibia catalyst that carried the stock for a year (the Mopane stake sale to TotalEnergies) closed in late July: consumed. What remains is a 5.3x EV/EBITDA cash machine with a 3.35% yield, an active €250M buyback, modest net debt, and a realized beta near -0.7 against European equities — a genuine diversifier. That mix is worth owning at the EMA20 zone around 19.45, where the panel's risk/reward reads 3:1. It is not worth chasing under the 20-21 supply zone that just rejected the print.

business.overview: Galp is Portugal's integrated energy company: upstream production (Brazil pre-salt, now a reshaped Namibia position), refining and marketing in Iberia, and a growing renewables book. The July report guided full-year EBITDA to roughly €4bn against €3.31bn trailing, powered by refining margins. The Mopane transaction with TotalEnergies — a non-cash asset swap that closed around July 23: traded a concentrated exploration stake for positions in neighbouring blocks, de-risking the story at the cost of its lottery ticket.
business.moat: Iberian refining and retail density plus low-cost Brazilian barrels. Not a wide moat; a cash-conversion story with disciplined capital returns.
business.theme: European energy cash returns, refining strength funding dividends and buybacks.

earnings.beatNote: Five straight bottom-line beats (Q2 2025 verified separately: €0.24 vs €0.16). The honest asterisk on the latest one: revenue missed widely, EBITDA came in a touch light (€1.27bn vs €1.28bn consensus), and tax effects helped the EPS line — which is exactly why the stock fell on a beat-and-raise day. Next report: October 26.

capitalStructure.atm: None: no ATM, no equity shelf, no convertibles found (verified at the source; foreign issuer, EDGAR is blind here)
capitalStructure.shareHistory: Shrinking: the completed prior buyback cancelled 16.5M shares on March 23 (capital reduced 753.5M → 737.0M); a €250M 2026 program has been running since March 2

technicals.setupNote: The structure survived its own bad news: after the 20.96 post-guidance top on July 23, the flush stopped at 19.01 on July 27; above the EMA50, and the EMA20 was reclaimed within two sessions. Price now sits 1% above the EMA20 with the full stack rising underneath (19.54 > 19.32 > 18.34). Overhead, 20.00-21.00 is proven supply. The clean trade is the retest: 19.40-19.50 holding puts three rising averages under the position with the supply zone as the first target.

macro.regime: Risk-on (VIX 15.9). ISM services Aug 5, US jobs report Aug 7.
macro.impact: Galp's earnings lever is refining margins and crude marks, not US rates — its realized beta against European equities is negative (~-0.7). That makes it the one name in this cohort that can go up on a day the tape goes down. The flip side: a sharp crude selloff hits the guidance that just got raised.

risks.riskSummary: The risks are about quality-of-catalyst, not solvency: a macro-made guidance raise that crude can unmake, a consumed Namibia story, a narrow float, and a supply zone sitting right on top of the price.

riskCards.title: Macro-Made Guidance
points: The ~€4bn EBITDA guide is driven by refining margins and price marks
A crude/margin selloff reverses the raise mechanically
The quarter itself missed on revenue and slightly on EBITDA
riskCards.verdict: You are long refining margins with a 3.4% coupon. Own it knowingly.

riskCards.title: Catalyst Vacuum After Mopane
points: The TotalEnergies swap closed ~July 23: the event the market waited a year for is done
The next dated catalyst is the October 26 report
Sell-the-news already expressed: -7.5% in two sessions from the top
riskCards.verdict: Without a date on the calendar, the stock needs the market to come to it; hence the pullback entry, not the chase.

riskCards.title: Float and Coverage
points: Free float ~45% (Amorim family and state-linked holders anchor the rest)
Foreign-listing data gaps: short interest and options surfaces effectively unserved
Thinner liquidity than the US names in this cohort (~1.8M shares/day)
riskCards.verdict: Size the position to the liquidity, not to the conviction.

tradeIdea.statusNote: No entry at 19.73 under the 20-21 supply zone that just rejected the print. This is a limit order at the EMA20 retest.
tradeIdea.entryNote: The 19.40-19.50 zone stacks the EMA20 (19.54, falling toward it), the post-flush consolidation floor and round-number support. Enter on a hold of that zone, not on the first touch. If 20.30 breaks on a closing basis before the pullback fills, the breakout path is valid at half size with a stop under 19.54.
tradeIdea.thesis: A 5.3x EV/EBITDA cash machine with a freshly raised guide, a 3.4% growing dividend and a shrinking share count, priced for skepticism after a sell-the-news fade. The trade buys that skepticism at the EMA20 with a stop under the July floor, and sells back into the supply that created it.
